findings.reason: the plan must name `skills/reckon-build/` as its file set and grep target, or its central done-when measures the absence of a directory rather than the absence of the prohibition.
findings.text: the plan's §2 table and §5 name `skills/reckon-ship/SKILL.md`, `skills/reckon-ship/references/worker-protocol.md` and `skills/reckon-ship/references/sprint-orchestration.md` as the files to edit, and the §2 done-when greps `skills/reckon-ship/`; that directory does not exist — `git ls-tree -r HEAD` carries no `reckon-ship` path, and 790d5c571 ("refactor(skills): rename reckon-ship to reckon-build, with no alias") already renamed it — so the done-when's "grep returns zero" is satisfied by an absent directory and the worker would report a false pass

findings.reason: the plan's file set must name `tests/test_skill_contracts.py:811` and migrate its literal assertions onto the derived expectation, otherwise two authorities assert one rule and the literal copy drifts unwatched.
findings.text: `test_ship_keeps_the_orchestrator_as_the_only_plan_state_writer` already pins the same landing-contract sentences as literals ("Workers author their own landing record in the same beat", "may edit or append to it", "Never mutate the shared project index, sprint state"), and §2's "Landed" note confirms it was this sibling the change re-aimed; the plan then adds `tests/test_skill_contract_parity.py` as a second, prompt-derived surface for the same sentences, so the repo carries both the drift-proof mechanism and the literal copies the plan's own docstring calls the defect

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no module; its single mechanism is a prompt-derived parity check that hides the derive-and-assert behaviour behind one small interface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan adds `tests/test_skill_contract_parity.py` while the established skill-contract owner `tests/test_skill_contracts.py:811` keeps literal-pinned copies of the same contract sentences the parity test derives.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's prior-art file set names `skills/reckon-ship/`, which does not exist in the repository; the landing-contract machinery it edits lives under `skills/reckon-build/`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the skill clauses are a deliberate verbatim mirror of the runtime prompt, with the reason stated (§4: the prompt is owned by another plan) and a drift guard, not an unjustified thin layer.
